newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline tumbles on views of ample supply.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline tumbles on views of ample supply.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline tumbled early session Wednesday after oil inventory data showed a surprising build in gasoline stocks and an oil industry's trade group said gasoline stocks were sufficient enough to meet even the most aggressive demand estimates.
"The fall is definitely API related. Also, open interest reached 100,000 for the first time in a long time, so people wanted to lighten their positions anyway," said Rocky D'Esposito of RJ Futures.
At 1045 EDT, May gasoline was off 1.50 cents at 60.40 cents a gallon, near its session low of 60.20 cents.

"We are testing a key technical support level of 60.00 cents (in gasoline), and we will see if we hold. The new Tosco facility will be up soon, and that has created a real bearish environment," said a New York refined products trader.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Wednesday in its annual outlook for the summer peak driving season that U.S. gasoline supplies should be sufficient to accomodate a 2.5 percent growth rate in demand, which is the upper range of estimates.
May heating oil was off 1.30 cents a gallon at 53.55 cents. May crude was off 36 cents $19.47 a barrel.
At April 14, gasoline open interest stood at 100,854 and rose above 100,000 late last month for first time since April 1994 as traders anticipated the strong gasoline demand season of spring summer.
But, in its oil inventory data for the week ended April 11, the API said gasoline stocks swelled 3.63 million barrels compared with a one to two million barrel decline expected by traders.
The build was due to implied demand falling to a seasonally weak 7.3 million barrels per day (bpd) compared with 8.1 million bpd the week before.

More gasoline supply is expected in the coming months when Tosco Corp's is seen restarting its Trainer, Pennsylvania refinery early summer after a $50 million modernization of the plant. In fact, the API cited the Trainer refinery restart as part of its gasoline supply/demand assessment.
The refinery will have a crude distillation capacity of 150,000 bpd, along with improved gasoline output efficiency.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
